entries.name: Aroon trend
entries.idea: Aroon indicator (Tushar Chande, 1995): reads how recently a market made its highest high and lowest low. A recent high with an old low is a young uptrend.
entries.why: A published trend rule with one parameter that is different from the moving-average, breakout and momentum rules already in the library: it looks at the age of the extremes, not the distance from an average.

reasons: Risk-adjusted (Sharpe) it did not beat simply holding BTC over the same out-of-sample period.
Could not rule out luck: with 21 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.69 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: ADX trend (Wilder)
entries.idea: Welles Wilder's Directional Movement Index (1978): ADX measures how strong a trend is and +DI / -DI which side is pushing. The classic rule enters only when the trend is strong and pointing up.
entries.why: A published trend-strength rule with settings fixed by its author (14 bars, 25 level). Unlike the moving-average and breakout rules in the library it trades only when the trend is strong, so it tests whether filtering by trend strength helps.

reasons: Risk-adjusted (Sharpe) it did not beat simply holding BTC over the same out-of-sample period.
Could not rule out luck: with 22 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.76 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: Parabolic SAR (Wilder)
entries.idea: Welles Wilder's Parabolic SAR (1978): a stop-and-reverse level that trails the trend and speeds up toward price as the trend ages; the classic rule is long while price is above it.
entries.why: A published trailing-stop trend rule with settings fixed by its author (step 0.02, maximum 0.2). Unlike the entry rules already tracked, the SAR is itself the exit, so it tests whether an accelerating trailing exit improves on slower exits.

reasons: Risk-adjusted (Sharpe) it did not beat simply holding BTC over the same out-of-sample period.
Could not rule out luck: with 23 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.98 (it needs to be above 0).
It took part in 51% of buy and hold's down bars but only 51% of its up bars, so timing did not help.

entries.name: Ichimoku cloud (9, 26, 52)
entries.idea: Ichimoku cloud (9, 26, 52): long while the close is above both cloud edges, with the cloud drawn 26 bars ahead so it never uses later data; exit below the cloud.
entries.why: A widely used all-in-one trend system from Japan (Hosoda, 1968). Fixed standard settings from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

reasons: Could not rule out luck: with 24 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.38 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: Time-series momentum (12 minus 1)
entries.idea: Time-series momentum (12 minus 1): long while the return from 365 bars ago to 30 bars ago is positive; flat otherwise.
entries.why: The best-known academic momentum rule (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen, 2012): a year of past return, skipping the latest month. Fixed settings from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

luck_check.note: Too few out-of-sample trades (3; at least 15 are needed) to run a luck check.

reasons: Only 3 trades out of sample (fewer than 15): too few to tell skill from luck.

entries.name: Keltner channel breakout
entries.idea: Keltner channel breakout: enter on a close above EMA(20) + 2 x ATR(10); exit on a close below EMA(20).
entries.why: A classic volatility-channel breakout from the strategy queue with fixed standard settings, chosen before any BTC result was seen. It is a close relative of the existing volatility channel rule (ATR 10 instead of 14), so the two are not independent tests.

reasons: Risk-adjusted (Sharpe) it did not beat simply holding BTC over the same out-of-sample period.
Could not rule out luck: with 26 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.62 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: Vortex indicator (14)
entries.idea: Vortex indicator (14): long while VI+ is above VI-; flat otherwise.
entries.why: A trend-direction indicator from Botes and Siepman (2010), built from how far each bar reaches past the previous bar. Fixed standard 14-bar setting from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

reasons: Could not rule out luck: with 27 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.10 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: Stochastic pullback in an uptrend
entries.idea: Stochastic pullback in an uptrend: enter when %K (14, smoothed 3) crosses up through 20 while the close is above its 200-bar average; exit when %K rises above 80.
entries.why: A classic dip-buying rule (Lane's stochastic oscillator) restricted to uptrends. Fixed standard settings from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

entries.name: Money Flow Index reversion
entries.idea: Money Flow Index (14) reversion: enter when MFI falls below 20; exit when it rises above 70.
entries.why: A volume-weighted cousin of RSI (Quong and Soudack), testing whether volume-backed exhaustion marks dips. Fixed standard levels from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

luck_check.note: Too few out-of-sample trades (6; at least 15 are needed) to run a luck check.

reasons: Only 6 trades out of sample (fewer than 15): too few to tell skill from luck.

entries.name: Commodity Channel Index trend
entries.idea: Commodity Channel Index (20) trend: enter when CCI rises above +100; exit when it falls below 0.
entries.why: A classic momentum-breakout reading from Lambert (1980), used here to follow strong pushes. Fixed standard levels from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

reasons: Could not rule out luck: with 30 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.54 (it needs to be above 0).

entries.name: On-balance volume trend
entries.idea: On-balance volume trend: long while OBV is above its 50-bar average and the close is above its 50-bar average; flat when either fails.
entries.why: Granville's classic volume-confirmation idea: price strength counts only when volume is flowing in with it. Fixed 50-bar settings from the strategy queue, chosen before any BTC result was seen.

reasons: Could not rule out luck: with 31 strategies in the library to pick from, the safe lower estimate of its Sharpe ratio is -0.53 (it needs to be above 0).
